questions.question: The dimension formula of which of the following is the same as the formula of impulse?
questions.questionHtml: The dimension formula of which of the following is the same as the formula of impulse?

options.text: Change in the rate of momentum
options.html: Change in the rate of momentum

questions.solution: Impulse has the same dimensional formula as momentum, [M][L][T-1]. Impulse is calculated as Force × Time, and momentum is Mass × Velocity. Both expressions result in identical dimensions. Other options like volume, torque, and change in momentum rate have distinct dimensional formulas and differ from impulse.

questions.question: Arrange the following post-World War II political developments in India in chronological order: 1. Cripps Mission 2. Wavell Plan & Shimla Conference 3. August Offer 4. Cabinet Mission
questions.questionHtml:
Arrange the following post-World War II political developments in India in chronological order:

1. Cripps Mission

2. Wavell Plan & Shimla Conference

3. August Offer

4. Cabinet Mission

options.html: 3 - 2 - 1 - 4

questions.solution:
The correct answer is (a) 3 - 1 - 2 - 4

Key Points

Chronological Order of Events:

  • August Offer (1940):
    • Proposed Dominion Status after the war.
    • Rejected by the Congress as it lacked immediate independence guarantees.
  • Cripps Mission (March 1942):
    • Sent by British PM Winston Churchill to secure Indian cooperation in WWII.
    • Offered Dominion Status and the right to draft a Constitution post-war.
    • Rejected by the Congress; led to the Quit India Movement (August 1942).
  • Wavell Plan & Shimla Conference (June-July 1945):
    • Proposed by Viceroy Lord Wavell to restructure the Viceroy’s Executive Council with an Indian-majority government.
    • Failed due to the Muslim League's insistence on being the sole representative of Indian Muslims.
  • Cabinet Mission (March 1946):
    • Sent to frame a plan for India's independence.
    • Proposed a Union of India with groupings of provinces.
    • Congress and Muslim League initially accepted but later disagreed on interpretations, leading to Partition.

questions.question: Day and Nights are caused by 1. rotation of the earth on its axis 2. revolution of the earth around the sun 3. inclination of earth's axis
questions.questionHtml:
Day and Nights are caused by
1. rotation of the earth on its axis
2. revolution of the earth around the sun
3. inclination of earth's axis
questions.solution:
The correct answer is rotation of the earth on its axis.

Key Points

  • Day and night are caused due to the rotation of the Earth on its axis.
  • The Earth completes one full rotation approximately every 24 hours, leading to the cycle of day and night.
  • The side of the Earth facing the Sun experiences daytime, while the opposite side experiences nighttime.
  • The axis of Earth's rotation is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, but this tilt does not directly cause day and night; it affects the variation in daylight hours across seasons.
  • The revolution of Earth around the Sun and the inclination of Earth's axis contribute to seasonal changes, not the day-night cycle.

Additional Information

  • Rotation: The spinning of the Earth on its axis, taking approximately 24 hours to complete one rotation.
  • Axis: An imaginary line passing through the Earth's North and South Poles, around which the Earth rotates.
  • Revolution: The Earth's orbital movement around the Sun, taking about 365.25 days to complete one revolution.
  • Inclination of Earth's Axis: The 23.5-degree tilt of the Earth's axis relative to its orbit around the Sun, which causes seasonal variations.
  • Seasonal Impact: While the Earth's rotation causes day and night, the tilt and revolution influence the length of days and nights over the course of a year, resulting in seasons.

questions.question: Which Gupta emperor was known as the 'Napoleon of India' due to his military conquests and strategic warfare?
questions.questionHtml: Which Gupta emperor was known as the 'Napoleon of India' due to his military conquests and strategic warfare?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Samudragupta.

Key Points

  • Samudragupta, a ruler of the Gupta dynasty, is often referred to as the 'Napoleon of India' because of his remarkable military achievements and strategic warfare skills.
  • He undertook extensive military campaigns to expand the Gupta Empire, which covered a major portion of the Indian subcontinent during his reign.
  • Samudragupta's conquests included regions in North India, Central India, and parts of South India.
  • He defeated numerous kings and established his authority over a vast empire, showcasing his strong military prowess.
  • Samudragupta was also known for his policy of ‘Dharmavijaya’ (victory through righteousness), which emphasized winning people's loyalty and respect rather than mere territorial conquest.
  • His achievements were recorded in the Allahabad Pillar Inscription, composed by his court poet, Harisena.
  • Besides his military accomplishments, Samudragupta was a patron of arts and culture. He was an accomplished musician and supported various forms of creative expression.
  • Samudragupta's reign is considered the golden age of Indian history, marked by significant advancements in administration, culture, and economic prosperity.

Additional Information

  • Chandragupta I
    • Chandragupta I was the founder of the Gupta Empire and reigned around 320 CE.
    • He laid the foundation for the Gupta dynasty by consolidating territories and forming alliances through marriage, notably with the Lichchhavi dynasty.
    • His reign marked the beginning of the Gupta calendar, an important historical landmark.
  • Kumaragupta
    • Kumaragupta I was another notable ruler of the Gupta dynasty who ruled during the 5th century CE.
    • He is famous for establishing the Nalanda University, one of the ancient world's most renowned centers of learning.
    • Despite facing challenges from external invasions, Kumaragupta maintained the stability of the empire during his reign.
  • Skandagupta
    • Skandagupta was a Gupta emperor who is known for his military defense against the Huna invasions.
    • He succeeded in repelling the Hunas and ensured the security of the Gupta Empire during his reign.
    • Skandagupta is also credited with maintaining the administrative and economic stability of the empire despite external threats.

questions.question: The Peninsular Plateau of India is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth and was once part of the ancient supercontinent known as ______.
questions.questionHtml: The Peninsular Plateau of India is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth and was once part of the ancient supercontinent known as ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Gondwanaland.

Key Points

  • The Peninsular Plateau of India is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth.
  • It was once part of the ancient supercontinent called Gondwanaland, which existed during the Late Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras (approximately 600 million years ago).
  • Gondwanaland included the landmasses of present-day South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.
  • The breakup of Gondwanaland led to the formation of the continents as we know them today, including the Indian landmass.
  • The Peninsular Plateau is characterized by its stable geological structure, which includes ancient rocks and formations such as igneous and metamorphic rocks.
  • This region is known for its rich mineral deposits, including coal, iron ore, manganese, and bauxite, which are important for India's economy.
  • The plateau has a rugged terrain with prominent features like the Deccan Plateau, Malwa Plateau, Chotanagpur Plateau, and Vindhya Range.
  • The geological history of Gondwanaland explains the presence of similar flora, fauna, and fossil records across the continents that were once part of this supercontinent.

Additional Information

  • Laurasia
    • Laurasia was another ancient supercontinent that existed alongside Gondwanaland.
    • It consisted of present-day North America, Europe, and Asia (excluding the Indian subcontinent).
    • Laurasia and Gondwanaland together formed the larger supercontinent called Pangaea before splitting apart.
  • Angaraland
    • Angaraland refers to the northern part of Laurasia, primarily comprising Siberia and other regions in northern Asia.
    • It is geologically distinct from Gondwanaland and is associated with the formation of the Ural Mountains.
  • Eurasia
    • Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia that exists today.
    • It is not an ancient supercontinent but a term used to describe the modern geographical and geopolitical region.

questions.question: Consider the following statement regarding GDP deflator: 1. When the GDP deflator is less than unity, nominal GDP is less than real GDP. 2. GDP deflator is available only annually with a long lag over one year and hence has very limited policy use. Which of the statement given above is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statement regarding GDP deflator:

1. When the GDP deflator is less than unity, nominal GDP is less than real GDP.

2. GDP deflator is available only annually with a long lag over one year and hence has very limited policy use.

Which of the statement given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.

Key PointsGDP deflator:

  • The ratio of nominal to real GDP is called GDP Deflator.
  • It is a more comprehensive measure of inflation.
  • The GDP deflator, also called implicit price deflator, is a measure of inflation.
  • It is the ratio of the value of goods and services an economy produces in a particular year at current prices to that of prices that prevailed during the base year.
  • GDP deflector is not formed on a fixed basket of goods and services.
  • This ratio helps show the extent to which the increase in the gross domestic product has happened on account of higher prices rather than an increase in output.
  • The deflator is a more comprehensive measure of inflation because it covers the entire range of goods and services produced in the economy.
  • The formula to find the GDP price deflator:
    • GDP price deflator = (nominal GDP ÷ real GDP) x 100. 
    • When nominal GDP is less than real GDP, then GDP deflator is less than unity and it means there is deflation in the country. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • GDP deflator is available only on a quarterly basis along with GDP estimates. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
  • Changes in consumption patterns or the introduction of goods and services are automatically reflected in the GDP deflator.
  • This allows the GDP deflator to absorb changes to an economy’s consumption or investment patterns.
  • Often, the trends of the GDP deflator will be similar to that of the CPI.
  • It is useful in identifying the inflated price levels and by how much over a specific period of time.
  • It includes goods and services produced domestically i.e. India. It does not include other goods or services produced outside the country.

questions.solution:
E-commerce Rules -2021:
  • The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 regulate commercial transactions between Indian retailers and overseas consumers, prohibiting online marketplaces from holding inventory or influencing product prices. Hence, Statement 1 is not correct.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes aims to benefit the minority youths who do not have a formal school leaving certificate?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following schemes aims to benefit the minority youths who do not have a formal school leaving certificate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nai Manzil.

Key Points

  • Nai Manzil is a scheme launched by the Government of India to provide education and skill training to minority youth who lack formal school leaving certificates.
  • The scheme aims to integrate minority youth into mainstream education and employment by bridging their academic and skill gaps.
  • It offers bridge courses equivalent to Class 8 or 10 from recognized institutions such as National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) or other state boards.
  • In addition to education, the program focuses on skill development in various trades to enhance employability.
  • The scheme is implemented through various project implementing agencies (PIAs) and has specific targets for women and marginalized groups within minority communities.

Additional Information

  • Target Beneficiaries: The scheme is aimed at minority communities, including Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains, with a special focus on youth aged 17–35 years.
  • Skill Development: The training programs under Nai Manzil are aligned with National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) to ensure quality and standardization.
  • Funding: The scheme is funded by the Ministry of Minority Affairs and partially supported by the World Bank.
  • Gender Inclusion: At least 30% of the beneficiaries under the Nai Manzil scheme must be women to promote gender equity.
  • Implementation: The scheme is executed through partnerships with educational and vocational institutions, ensuring that the beneficiaries receive both academic qualifications and employable skills.

questions.question: What was the direct cause of the rise of Extremism in the Indian National Movement?
questions.questionHtml: What was the direct cause of the rise of Extremism in the Indian National Movement?

options.text: The Govt. did not pay heed to moderates.
options.html: The Govt. did not pay heed to moderates.

options.text: Oppression by the Britishers on the Indians.
options.html: Oppression by the Britishers on the Indians.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Partition of Bengal.

Important Points

  • The Partition of Bengal was the direct cause of the Rise of Extremism in the Indian National Movement.
  • The partition of Bengal in 1905 opened the eyes of the Indians to the true colors of the British rulers.
  • The extremist leaders were also influenced by the growth of spiritual nationalism at that time.
  • The extremist goal was ‘swaraj’.
  • Extremist leaders are Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Aurobindo Ghosh, Rajnarayan Bose, A K Dutt, V O C Pillai.


Additional Information

  • The Partition of Bengal was the decision of separating eastern parts of Bengal from the rest of Bengal.
  • On 20th July 1905, Lord Curzon announced the partition of the undivided Bengal Presidency.
  • The Presidency was the most populous province in India, with around 8 crore people, and comprised the present-day states of West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, parts of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Assam, as well as today’s Bangladesh.
  • It was partitioned due to following reason
    • To break the growing strength of Bengali nationalism since Bengal was the base of Indian nationalism.
    • To divide the Hindus and Muslims in Bengal.
    • To show the enormous power of the British Government is doing whatever it liked.

questions.question: Which of the following is defined as the ratio of liquid assets to net demand and time liabilities?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is defined as the ratio of liquid assets to net demand and time liabilities?
questions.solution: The correct answer to the given problem is the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR). It is the reserve requirement that commercial banks in India must maintain in the form of cash, gold reserves, and government-approved securities before providing credit to customers. By changing the level of SLR, the Reserve Bank of India can increase or decrease bank credit expansion. If the SLR is reduced, banks have more money to lend, which may lead to a decrease in lending rates. By reducing the level of SLR, the RBI can increase liquidity with commercial banks, resulting in increased investment, which fuels growth and demand. On the other hand, Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is a general name for any theory of the corporation that emphasizes both the responsibility to make money and the responsibility to interact ethically with the surrounding community. CSR is composed of four obligations: ecological responsibility, legal responsibility, social responsibility, and philanthropic responsibility.

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), who can be held liable for abetment of an offense?
questions.questionHtml: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), who can be held liable for abetment of an offense?

options.text: Only a person who helps physically
options.html: Only a person who helps physically

options.text: Anyone who aids, counsels, or instigates the offense
options.html: Anyone who aids, counsels, or instigates the offense

options.text: Only persons who are present at the scene
options.html: Only persons who are present at the scene

options.text: Only the person who directly commits the crime
options.html: Only the person who directly commits the crime

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Anyone who aids, counsels, or instigates the offense.

Key Points

  • Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, abetment of an offense includes aiding, counseling, or instigating the commission of a crime.
  • The term "abetment" is defined broadly to encompass both direct and indirect involvement in encouraging or facilitating a crime.
  • A person can be held liable for abetment even if they are not physically present at the crime scene but have contributed to its commission through advice, encouragement, or other means.
  • The BNS, 2023, replaces the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and retains the concept of abetment, which was earlier encapsulated in Section 107 of the IPC.
  • This provision ensures accountability for individuals who play a role in the planning or instigation of crimes, even if they do not physically execute the act themselves.

Additional Information

  • Option 1: Only a person who helps physically
    • This is incorrect. Abetment is not limited to physical assistance; it also includes emotional or intellectual support, such as giving advice or encouragement.
    • Physical help may be a form of abetment, but it is not the only criterion under the law.
  • Option 3: Only persons who are present at the scene
    • Being present at the crime scene is not a mandatory condition for abetment.
    • Individuals can be held liable for abetment even if they are not physically present but have contributed to the offense through their actions or words.
  • Option 4: Only the person who directly commits the crime
    • This is incorrect because abetment focuses on those who assist, instigate, or encourage the commission of a crime, not just the primary perpetrator.
    • The person who directly commits the crime is the principal offender, while those who aid or instigate are abettors.
  • About Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023
    • The BNS, 2023, is a proposed legislation that seeks to replace the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which has been in effect since 1860.
    • It aims to modernize criminal laws in India, making them more relevant to contemporary societal needs.
    • The new code emphasizes justice, accountability, and deterrence while retaining several essential principles from the IPC.
    • Key provisions under the BNS include updated definitions of crimes, streamlined procedures, and a focus on victim-centric justice.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about Brahadeeshwarar temple. 1. It is a Shiva temple at Thanjavur and also called as the Rajarajeswara temple. 2. It was completed by Karikalan Chola I. Which among the above statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements about Brahadeeshwarar temple.

1. It is a Shiva temple at Thanjavur and also called as the Rajarajeswara temple.

2. It was completed by Karikalan Chola I.

Which among the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.

Key Points

  • The Shiva temple of Thanjavur is also called the Rajarajeswara or Brahadeeshwarar temple. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • It was completed around 1009 by Rajaraja Chola. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

Additional Information

  • Temple building was prolific at this time, and over a hundred important temples of the Chola period are in a good state of preservation.
  • This temple is bigger in scale than anything built by their predecessors, the Pallavas, Chalukyas or Pandyas.
  • This temple's pyramidal multi-storeyed vimana rises a massive, 70-metre structure topped by a monolithic shikhara which is an octagonal dome-shaped stupika.
  • It is in this temple that one notices for the first time two large gopuras (gateway towers) with an elaborate sculptural programme which was conceived along with the temple.
  • Huge Nandi figures are also found the corners of the shikhara, and the kalasha on top by itself is about three metres and eight centimetres in height.
  • Hundreds of stucco figures decorate the vimana, although it is possible that some of these may have been added on during the Maratha Period and did not always belong to the Chola Period.

questions.question: What type of reaction occurs when limestone gets converted into quicklime on heating?
questions.questionHtml: What type of reaction occurs when limestone gets converted into quicklime on heating?
questions.solution: Heating limestone (CaCO₃) causes it to decompose into quicklime (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂), making it a decomposition reaction where one compound breaks into simpler substances.
